A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same credal-wrapper research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the revised title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original OOD-detection and calibration experiments, architecture comparisons, and ensemble-size and approximation-parameter ablations in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds EDD comparisons, BNN sampling experiments, overconfidence tests, NLL evaluations, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The probability bounds, credal-set construction, PIA algorithm, and intersection prediction remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 adds an optional generalized Hartley EU-scoring variant, replacing the entropy difference in that experiment without changing the underlying wrapper or trained models.

E1.justification: The CIFAR10/100, SVHN, Tiny-ImageNet, corrupted CIFAR, and ImageNet/ImageNet-O coverage is retained. Appendix A.6 adds a controlled overconfident-member scenario, supplying the wrapper with one artificially one-hot prediction among five ensemble predictions. This extends the tested prediction-input conditions without adding an image dataset.

E2.justification: v1 compares wrapped models with classical BNNR, BNNF, and deep ensembles. v2 adds the distinct Ensemble Distribution Distillation comparator family: EDD appears in Table 1 and Figure 2, while EDD-Fair, using the baseline learning-rate schedule, is evaluated in Table 19. The original comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds BNN sampling settings of 10, 50, and 1000 predictions, EDD training under two schedules, a one-hot prediction intervention, accuracy and clean-data calibration evaluation, and corrupted-data NLL evaluation. These are additional protocols; the original five-sample settings, dataset splits, and documented baseline training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses examine BNN sample counts, alternative GH uncertainty scoring, overconfident ensemble members, individual prediction cases, ID/OOD uncertainty distributions, and inference-cost tradeoffs. Appendix A.10 also adds distributions explaining PIA sensitivity. The earlier ensemble-size and PIA ablations remain, while relocated TU results are not new analyses.

E5.justification: The retained experiments continue reporting 15 runs and numerical spreads. New computational-cost studies in Tables 15–17 explicitly use 20-run averaging, with spreads for inference times. This adds repeated-measurement information without establishing an increase in runs for the original experiments.

E6.justification: Original tabulated OOD scores are retained, including TU results relocated to the appendix. v2 adds substantial accuracy, calibration, EDD, sampling, GH, overconfidence, NLL, and runtime results. It also changes the retained PIA timing units: 7.182 seconds in v1 Table 6 becomes 7.182 milliseconds in v2 Table 4. This is a reported-value revision, not evidence of an algorithmic speedup.

T1.justification: Appendices A.4 and C add mathematical treatment of GH scoring, lower probabilities, Möbius inversion, coherence, and credal-set vertices. Appendix D introduces a full-simplex-support assumption and an asymptotic argument that the intersection prediction approaches uniformity. These substantially extend v1's formal material; the clarified normalization notation alone would not constitute such a change.

C1.justification: The abstracts, contribution statements, and conclusions retain the same central claims: constructing a credal wrapper from finite BNN or ensemble predictions improves uncertainty estimation, and intersection probabilities improve calibration on corrupted data. The title's classification wording reflects a scope already stated in v1 rather than a new central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 newly discusses convergence toward uniform predictions under full support, distinguishes finite-sample benefits from BMA convergence, and explains entropy-range versus GH uncertainty. It also interprets overconfidence as expanding the credal set, small PIA settings as underestimating uncertainty, and fewer predictive samples as potentially offsetting wrapper overhead. These materially expand mechanisms and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 adds EDD training details, including temperature annealing and scheduler variants, and specifies hardware for the new timing studies. A reproducibility statement and GitLab code link replace v1's supplementary-files statement. Original training details remain, although the explicit OOD-scoring pseudocode is removed while its verbal procedure is retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against evidential and Dirichlet-based methods, discussing prior/posterior networks, EDD, and critiques by Ulmer and Juergens. It adds CreINNs and convex-hull/coherence comparisons, while removing v1's discussion of Javanmardi's conformalized credal predictors. These are substantive changes beyond citation-style or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The introduction is rewritten and reordered, and Section 4 integrates calibration discussion into the dataset and architecture evaluations instead of retaining a separate ECE section. TU evaluation moves to the appendix, the PIA study moves into the main text, and an appendix contents list and new discussion sections reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: Existing EU/TU tables and plots are split and redistributed, Table 1 gains prediction-performance columns and EDD rows, and ECE panels become compact horizontal strips. v2 adds prediction visualizations, uncertainty-density plots, NLL plots, timing tables, and a convex-hull illustration. The original intersection-probability schematic and OOD-scoring pseudocode display are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evaluation and transparency through EDD comparisons, clean-data accuracy/calibration results, targeted robustness studies, and Appendix D's explicit asymptotic limitation. These address important gaps in v1's mainly OOD/ECE-based validation and expose tradeoffs rather than merely adding favorable scores. The unexplained seconds-to-milliseconds timing revision limits confidence in the cost reporting, but the broader evidence and clearer applicability boundaries provide a substantial net improvement.
